title: Where Did the Stars Go?
subtitle: 星星去哪了？光害讓夜空變亮
source: 原創教學文章；研究內容依 Kyba et al.（2023）Science 原始論文及作者訪談報導，2026-10-21 核對

sources.title: Kyba, C. C. M., Altıntaş, Y. Ö., Walker, C. E., & Newhouse, M. (2023). Citizen scientists report global rapid reductions in the visibility of stars from 2011 to 2022. Science, 379(6629).
SpaceNews (2023-01-20). The visibility of stars in the night sky has declined faster than previously thought.

beginner.title: Counting Stars
paras: Go outside on a clear night and look up. How many stars can you see? If you live in a city, maybe only a few. Your grandparents may remember a sky full of stars. Where did they go? The stars are still there. The problem is the light we make at night.
在晴朗的夜晚走到戶外，抬頭看看，你能看到幾顆星星？如果你住在城市裡，也許只有幾顆。你的祖父母可能還記得滿天星斗的夜空。星星都去哪了？它們其實還在那裡，問題出在我們夜裡製造的光。

Streetlights, signs, buildings and screens all send light into the sky. This light makes the night sky brighter, so faint stars disappear. Scientists call this light pollution. This kind of pollution does not make the air dirty, but it hides the sky from us. To measure it, they asked ordinary people around the world for help.
路燈、招牌、建築和螢幕，都把光送進天空。這些光讓夜空變亮，於是比較暗的星星就看不見了。科學家稱之為「光害」。這種污染不會讓空氣變髒，卻把天空藏了起來。為了測量光害，他們請全世界的一般民眾幫忙。

In a project called Globe at Night, people looked at the sky and compared it with star maps. Then they reported how many stars they could see. Between 2011 and 2022, people sent in more than 51,000 reports. Scientists studied these reports and published the results in 2023. You do not need a telescope to take part. You only need your eyes and a clear night.
在一個叫做「Globe at Night（全球夜空觀測）」的計畫裡，人們看著天空，對照星圖，再回報自己看得到多少星星。從 2011 年到 2022 年，民眾送出了超過 51,000 筆回報。科學家分析了這些回報，並在 2023 年發表了結果。參加這個計畫不需要望遠鏡，只需要你的眼睛和一個晴朗的夜晚。

The results were surprising. On average, the night sky got brighter by almost 10 percent every year. If this continues, a child born in a place where 250 stars are visible may see only about 100 stars there on their 18th birthday. This change was much faster than scientists had expected.
結果令人驚訝：平均來說，夜空每年變亮將近 10%。如果這個趨勢持續下去，一個在看得到 250 顆星星的地方出生的孩子，到了 18 歲生日時，在那裡可能只看得到大約 100 顆。這個變化比科學家預期的快得多。

The good news is that light pollution is easy to reduce. We can turn off lights we do not need, point lights down instead of up, and use warmer, softer colors. Unlike many other kinds of pollution, light pollution disappears the moment we switch it off. Even small changes at home, like closing the curtains at night, can help.
好消息是，光害很容易減少。我們可以關掉不需要的燈，讓燈光往下照而不是往上照，並使用比較溫暖、柔和的顏色。和許多其他污染不同，光害在我們關燈的那一刻就消失了。即使是在家裡的小改變，像是晚上拉上窗簾，也能有幫助。

intermediate.title: Where Did the Stars Go?
paras: For most of human history, people could look up at night and see thousands of stars and the band of the Milky Way. Today, many people live under skies so bright that the Milky Way is invisible. The stars have not gone anywhere. What has changed is the amount of artificial light we send into the sky.
在人類歷史的大部分時間裡，人們在夜晚抬頭就能看到成千上萬顆星星，以及銀河那條光帶。如今，很多人生活在明亮到看不見銀河的夜空下。星星哪裡都沒去，改變的是我們送上天空的人造光。

This glow, known as skyglow, is a form of light pollution. It is difficult to measure accurately, partly because the satellites that photograph Earth at night do not detect all types of light equally well. To get a more complete picture, scientists turned to citizen science. Instead of relying only on machines, they asked people to use their own eyes.
這種光暈叫做「天空輝光」，是光害的一種形式。它很難準確測量，部分原因是在夜間拍攝地球的衛星，並不是對所有種類的光都同樣敏感。為了得到更完整的圖像，科學家求助於公民科學。他們不只依賴機器，而是請人們用自己的眼睛觀察。

Through a project called Globe at Night, volunteers around the world compared the night sky with a series of star charts and recorded which one matched what they could see. In a study published in Science in 2023, Christopher Kyba and his colleagues analysed 51,351 of these observations, collected between 2011 and 2022. Each report was simple, but together they formed a valuable record covering many countries and many years.
透過一個叫做「Globe at Night」的計畫，世界各地的志工把夜空和一系列星圖做比較，記下哪一張最符合自己看到的景象。在 2023 年發表於《科學》期刊的研究中，克里斯多福．凱巴與同事分析了 2011 到 2022 年間蒐集的 51,351 筆觀測資料。每一筆回報都很簡單，但加在一起，就形成了一份涵蓋許多國家、許多年份的寶貴紀錄。

The decline in visible stars suggested that the sky was brightening by 9.6 percent per year on average — fast enough to double the brightness in about eight years. Kyba explained what this means: if the trend continued, a child born where 250 stars were visible would be able to see only about 100 there by their 18th birthday. The rate was much faster than satellite measurements had suggested, possibly because of the switch to white LED lights, which satellites cannot fully detect. For people who love the night sky, it was a worrying result.
可見星星的減少顯示，夜空平均每年變亮 9.6%——快到大約八年就會亮一倍。凱巴解釋這代表什麼：如果這個趨勢持續，一個在看得到 250 顆星的地方出生的孩子，到 18 歲生日時，在那裡只能看到大約 100 顆。這個速度遠比衛星測量所顯示的快，原因可能是改用白色 LED 燈，而衛星無法完整偵測這類光。對熱愛夜空的人來說，這是一個令人擔憂的結果。

Light pollution is unusual among environmental problems because the solution is immediate. Shielding lights so they shine downward, using only as much light as needed, choosing warmer colours and turning lights off when they are not in use can all reduce skyglow overnight. The stars, after all, are still there — waiting for us to turn down the lights. Some towns and parks have already been recognised for protecting their dark skies.
在各種環境問題中，光害很特別，因為解決方法立刻就能見效。給燈加上遮罩讓光往下照、只使用需要的光量、選擇較暖的顏色，以及不用時關燈，都能在一夜之間減少天空輝光。畢竟，星星都還在——等著我們把燈調暗。有些城鎮和公園已經因為保護了它們的暗空而獲得肯定。

advanced.title: The Vanishing Night Sky
paras: The starry night sky is one of humanity’s oldest shared experiences. It guided travellers, structured calendars and inspired myths, science and poetry across every culture. Yet for a growing proportion of people, that experience is slipping away, not because anything has happened to the stars, but because of the artificial light we scatter into the atmosphere every night. For many children growing up in cities today, the Milky Way is something they have seen only in photographs.
滿天星斗的夜空，是人類最古老的共同經驗之一。它為旅人指路、構成曆法，也在每一種文化中激發了神話、科學與詩歌。然而，對越來越多人來說，這種經驗正在流失——不是因為星星出了什麼事，而是因為我們每晚散射到大氣中的人造光。對今天許多在城市長大的孩子來說，銀河是只在照片裡見過的東西。

Measuring this skyglow at a global scale has proved surprisingly difficult. The satellites that image Earth at night are most sensitive to light directed upward, whereas much of the glow that hides the stars comes from light emitted horizontally. They are also largely insensitive to the blue wavelengths emitted by the white LEDs that have replaced older orange street lamps in many cities. Satellite data alone, in other words, may be telling us only part of the story.
在全球尺度上測量天空輝光，結果出乎意料地困難。在夜間拍攝地球的衛星，對向上照射的光最敏感，但遮蔽星星的光暈，有很大一部分來自水平方向發出的光。衛星也幾乎無法偵測白色 LED 發出的藍光波段，而許多城市已用這種燈取代了舊式的橘色路燈。換句話說，光靠衛星資料，我們可能只看到了故事的一部分。

To address this gap, Christopher Kyba and colleagues turned to Globe at Night, a citizen science project in which volunteers compare the sky with a set of charts showing different numbers of stars. Their 2023 study in Science analysed 51,351 observations made between 2011 and 2022. Because the human eye is the instrument that actually experiences the night sky, these simple reports captured something satellites could not. Individual reports are imprecise, but tens of thousands of them, gathered over more than a decade, can reveal trends that no single observer would notice.

為了彌補這個缺口，凱巴與同事轉向「Globe at Night」——一個公民科學計畫，志工把天空和一組顯示不同星星數量的星圖做比較。他們 2023 年發表於《科學》期刊的研究，分析了 2011 到 2022 年間的 51,351 筆觀測。由於人眼才是真正體驗夜空的那個「儀器」，這些簡單的回報捕捉到了衛星捕捉不到的東西。個別回報並不精確，但十多年來累積的數萬筆回報，卻能揭露任何單一觀察者都察覺不到的趨勢。

The results were stark. The loss of visible stars corresponded to an average increase in sky brightness of 9.6 percent per year — equivalent to the sky doubling in brightness roughly every eight years, and far faster than the roughly 2 percent annual growth suggested by satellite observations. Over eighteen years, the authors noted, such a rate would reduce a location with 250 visible stars to one with 100. A child, in effect, could watch the sky fade over the course of growing up. The authors were careful to note that the trend varied by region, and that the figure was an average across the locations where participants happened to live.
結果令人震驚。可見星星的減少，相當於天空亮度平均每年增加 9.6%——大約每八年亮度就加倍，遠比衛星觀測所顯示的每年約 2% 成長快得多。作者指出，十八年下來，這樣的速度會讓一個原本看得到 250 顆星的地方，只剩下 100 顆。實際上，一個孩子可能在長大的過程中，親眼看著天空逐漸黯淡。作者也謹慎地指出，這個趨勢因地區而異，而且這個數字是參與者剛好居住的那些地點的平均值。

Unlike plastic in the ocean or carbon in the atmosphere, light pollution leaves no residue: it ends the instant a light is switched off or redirected. That makes it one of the most reversible environmental problems we face. Shielded fixtures that direct light downward, warmer colour temperatures, dimmers and timers are all inexpensive and widely available. The obstacle is less technological than cultural — a habit of treating brightness as safety and darkness as waste. Recovering the stars may begin with learning to value the dark. Few environmental victories could be achieved so quickly or so cheaply.
不像海洋裡的塑膠或大氣中的碳，光害不會留下殘餘物：燈一關掉或改變方向，它就立刻結束。這使它成為我們面對的環境問題中，最能逆轉的一種。讓光往下照的遮罩燈具、較暖的色溫、調光器和定時器，都便宜又容易取得。障礙與其說是技術上的，不如說是文化上的——一種把明亮當作安全、把黑暗當作浪費的習慣。要找回星星，也許得從學會珍惜黑暗開始。很少有環境上的勝利，能這麼快、這麼便宜地達成。

quote.text: If the stars should appear one night in a thousand years, how would men believe and adore; and preserve for many generations the remembrance of the city of God which had been shown!
quote.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to find stars with a telescope in a big city.
How the night sky is getting brighter and hiding the stars.
Why our grandparents saw fewer stars than we do.
How scientists send light into the sky to study stars.
beginner.evidence: On average, the night sky got brighter by almost 10 percent every year.
beginner.why: 全文說明光害讓夜空變亮、星星消失，以及怎麼改善。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 You do not need a telescope。
正反顛倒：祖父母那一代看得到更多星星。
張冠李戴：送光進天空的是街燈、招牌等，不是科學家。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “To measure it” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: A star map.
The night sky.
The air.
Light pollution.
beginner.why: 前一句：科學家稱之為光害，接著要測量的就是光害。
traps: 時序錯置：星圖是第三段的工具。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：天空是被照亮的對象。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：後一句說光害不會弄髒空氣。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: People sent in more than 51,000 reports between 2011 and 2022.
People needed a telescope to take part in Globe at Night.
The sky got brighter by almost 10 percent over twelve years.
Light pollution makes the air dirty and hard to breathe.
beginner.evidence: Between 2011 and 2022, people sent in more than 51,000 reports.
beginner.why: 第三段：2011 到 2022 年間有超過 51,000 筆回報。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 You do not need a telescope。
數字錯位：是「每年」將近 10%。
正反顛倒：原文 does not make the air dirty。

beginner.q: What makes light pollution different from many other kinds of pollution?
options: It is caused mainly by stars.
It can be seen only by scientists.
It disappears as soon as we turn the lights off.
It has been getting smaller every year.
beginner.evidence: light pollution disappears the moment we switch it off
beginner.why: 最後一段：關燈的那一刻光害就消失。
traps: 正反顛倒：星星是被遮住的，光害來自人造光。
正反顛倒：一般人用肉眼就能參與觀測。
正反顛倒：天空每年變亮。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Satellites give the most complete picture of the night sky.
The Milky Way has moved farther away from Earth.
Volunteers’ observations show skyglow is increasing faster than expected, but it can be reduced.
White LED lights help people see more stars at night.
intermediate.evidence: The rate was much faster than satellite measurements had suggested
intermediate.why: 第三、四段：志工觀測顯示天空變亮的速度比衛星估計快；第五段提出解法。
traps: 正反顛倒：第二段說衛星偵測不到所有光。
正反顛倒：原文 The stars have not gone anywhere。
正反顛倒：白光 LED 可能是天空變亮、但衛星測不到的原因。

intermediate.q: What does “citizen science” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: Research in which ordinary people help collect data.
Science lessons taught to citizens in schools.
Research paid for by city governments.
Studies of how cities use electricity.
intermediate.evidence: Instead of relying only on machines, they asked people to use their own eyes.
intermediate.why: 下一句解釋：請一般民眾用自己的眼睛觀測。
traps: 字面誤讀：不是公民課。
捏造：文中沒提經費。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：光害與城市有關，但不是這個詞的意思。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Globe at Night volunteers used telescopes to count stars.
The sky was getting brighter by 9.6 percent every eight years.
Satellites measured an even faster increase than the volunteers.
Kyba’s team analysed 51,351 observations collected over about a decade.
intermediate.evidence: Christopher Kyba and his colleagues analysed 51,351 of these observations, collected between 2011 and 2022
intermediate.why: 第三段：分析了 2011 到 2022 年的 51,351 筆觀測。
traps: 捏造：志工是拿天空和星圖比對。
數字錯位：每年 9.6%，約八年亮度加倍。
正反顛倒：衛星低估了增加的速度。

intermediate.q: Why might satellites have underestimated the brightening of the sky?
options: They were turned off between 2011 and 2022.
They cannot fully detect light from white LED lamps.
They measure the stars instead of artificial light.
They were used only in a few countries.
intermediate.evidence: possibly because of the switch to white LED lights, which satellites cannot fully detect
intermediate.why: 第四段：可能因為改用白光 LED，衛星偵測不完整。
traps: 時序錯置：2011–2022 是志工觀測的期間。
捏造：衛星拍的是地球夜間的光。
張冠李戴：涵蓋許多國家的是志工回報。

advanced.q: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
options: Bright Cities Are Safer Cities
How Satellites Measure Every Light on Earth
Why the Stars Are Moving Away From Us
The Fading Sky: What Volunteers Revealed About Light Pollution
advanced.evidence: these simple reports captured something satellites could not
advanced.why: 第三到五段：志工觀測揭露天空變亮得比衛星估計快，並指出光害是可逆的。
traps: 正反顛倒：作者批評「亮＝安全」的習慣。
正反顛倒：衛星偵測不到水平方向的光和藍光。
正反顛倒：原文 not because anything has happened to the stars。

advanced.q: What does the author mean by saying light pollution “leaves no residue”?
options: It cannot be measured by satellites at all.
It leaves nothing behind once the light is switched off.
It affects only people who live in cities.
It slowly builds up in the atmosphere over years.
advanced.evidence: light pollution leaves no residue: it ends the instant a light is switched off or redirected
advanced.why: 冒號後面解釋：關燈或改變方向的那一刻就結束，不會殘留。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：衛星的限制在第二段。
捏造：文中沒有這樣的限制。
正反顛倒：這是在形容塑膠或碳，光害正好相反。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The human eye is less able than satellites to see the night sky.
The trend was the same in every region where people took part.
Satellite observations suggested sky brightness grew by about 2 percent a year.
Older orange street lamps have replaced white LEDs in many cities.
advanced.evidence: far faster than the roughly 2 percent annual growth suggested by satellite observations
advanced.why: 第四段：衛星觀測顯示每年約 2%，遠低於 9.6%。
traps: 正反顛倒：人眼正是真正體驗夜空的「儀器」。
正反顛倒：原文 the trend varied by region。
時序顛倒：是白光 LED 取代了舊的橘色路燈。

advanced.q: What does the author suggest is the main obstacle to reducing light pollution?
options: The belief that brightness means safety and darkness is waste.
The high cost of shielded lights and timers.
The lack of technology to redirect light downward.
The difficulty of measuring skyglow from space.
advanced.evidence: The obstacle is less technological than cultural — a habit of treating brightness as safety and darkness as waste.
advanced.why: 第五段：障礙主要是文化，而不是技術。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 inexpensive and widely available。
正反顛倒：原文 less technological。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：測量困難是第二段的問題，不是減少光害的障礙。

reflections: Tonight, count how many stars you can see from your home. What lights near you might be making the sky brighter?
Some people feel safer with bright lights. How could a city reduce light pollution while still keeping people safe?

The satellites that photograph Earth at night are most sensitive to light directed upward, whereas much of the glow that hides the stars comes from light sent out sideways. They also miss much of the blue light from white LEDs, which have replaced older orange street lamps in many cities. Satellite data alone, in other words, may tell only part of the story.
要在全球尺度上測量這種光暈，困難得出奇。在夜間拍攝地球的衛星，對往上射的光最敏感，但遮住星星的光暈有很大一部分來自往側面射出的光。衛星也偵測不到白光 LED 發出的大部分藍光，而許多城市已經用白光 LED 取代了舊式的橘色路燈。換句話說，光靠衛星資料，可能只看到故事的一部分。

To fill this gap, Christopher Kyba and his colleagues turned to Globe at Night, a citizen science project (research in which ordinary people help collect data). Volunteers compare the night sky with a set of charts showing different numbers of stars and report which one matches what they see. In a 2023 study published in Science, the team analysed 51,351 such observations made between 2011 and 2022. Individual reports are imprecise, yet tens of thousands of them, gathered over more than a decade, can reveal trends that no single observer would notice.
為了補上這個缺口，凱巴和同事求助於「夜空地球」——一個公民科學計畫（由一般民眾協助蒐集資料的研究）。志工把夜空和一組顯示不同星星數量的星圖比對，回報哪一張最符合自己看到的。在 2023 年刊登於《科學》期刊的研究中，團隊分析了 2011 到 2022 年間的 51,351 筆觀測。單一筆回報並不精確，但十多年來累積的數萬筆，能揭露任何一個觀察者都察覺不到的趨勢。

The results were stark. The loss of visible stars suggested that the sky was growing brighter by 9.6 percent a year on average — so fast that its brightness would double in about eight years, and far faster than the roughly 2 percent a year suggested by satellites. At such a rate, a place where 250 stars are visible would show only about 100 after eighteen years. A child, in effect, could watch the sky fade while growing up. The authors noted, however, that the trend varied by region.
結果令人震驚。可見星星的減少顯示，天空平均每年變亮 9.6%——快到大約八年亮度就會加倍，也遠快於衛星顯示的每年約 2%。照這個速度，一個看得到 250 顆星星的地方，十八年後只看得到大約 100 顆。實際上，一個孩子可能在長大的過程中，親眼看著天空褪色。不過作者也指出，這個趨勢因地區而異。

Unlike plastic in the ocean, light pollution leaves nothing behind: it ends the instant a light is switched off or pointed downward. Shielded lamps, warmer colours, dimmers and timers are all cheap and widely available. The obstacle, then, is less technical than cultural — a habit of treating brightness as safety and darkness as waste. Only when we learn to value the dark will the stars return.
和海洋裡的塑膠不同，光害不會留下任何東西：燈一關掉或轉向下方，它就立刻結束。加遮罩的燈具、較暖的色溫、調光器和定時器，都便宜又容易取得。所以，障礙與其說是技術，不如說是文化——一種把明亮當成安全、把黑暗當成浪費的習慣。只有學會珍惜黑暗，星星才會回來。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How volunteers revealed a fast rise in light pollution.
How satellites photograph every light on Earth.
Why the stars are moving away from our planet.
How cities choose the colour of their street lamps.
questions.evidence: can reveal trends that no single observer would notice
questions.why: 全文：公民科學揭露天空變亮的速度遠快於衛星估計，並指出光害可逆。
traps: 正反顛倒：衛星漏掉了不少光。
正反顛倒：原文 The stars have not gone anywhere。
以偏概全：路燈只是衛星偵測不到藍光的原因。

questions.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “stark” in the fourth paragraph?
options: Hard to measure.
Calm and hopeful.
Clear and alarming.
Bright and colourful.
questions.why: 後面說天空八年亮度就加倍、孩子會看著天空褪色，可知結果「鮮明而令人憂心」。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：難以測量是第二段的問題。
正反顛倒：結果令人擔憂。
字面誤讀：bright 是天空變亮，不是 stark 的意思。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The trend was exactly the same in every region.
Satellites suggested a much slower rise in brightness.
Satellites are most sensitive to light sent sideways.
The 2023 study used reports collected over one year.
questions.evidence: far faster than the roughly 2 percent a year suggested by satellites
questions.why: 第四段：衛星顯示每年約 2%，志工資料是 9.6%。
traps: 正反顛倒：趨勢因地區而異。
正反顛倒：衛星對往上的光最敏感。
數字錯位：2011 到 2022 年，十多年。

questions.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Orange street lamps produce more blue light than LEDs.
Volunteers’ reports were more precise than satellites.
Light pollution is harder to remove than plastic.
Satellite records alone probably underestimated the problem.
questions.evidence: Satellite data alone, in other words, may tell only part of the story.
questions.why: 衛星漏掉側射光和藍光，數據又遠低於志工結果，可推知衛星低估了問題。
traps: 正反顛倒：藍光來自白光 LED。
正反顛倒：原文 Individual reports are imprecise。
正反顛倒：光害一關燈就結束，比塑膠容易處理。

mixed.prompt: Volunteers compared the night sky with [47] showing different numbers of stars, and their reports suggested that the sky was growing [48] by 9.6 percent a year.
mixed.why: 第一格出自第三段 a set of charts（複數）；第二格出自第四段 growing brighter（grow 加比較級）。

mixed.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage? Choose ALL that apply.
options: The team analysed 51,351 observations.
The observations were made between 2011 and 2022.
Satellites detect the blue light of white LEDs very well.
The trend was the same in every region.
At 9.6 percent a year, brightness doubles in about eight years.
Light pollution leaves a long-lasting residue.
mixed.why: A、B 第三段；E 第四段。C 正反顛倒（衛星漏掉藍光）；D 正反顛倒（因地區而異）；F 正反顛倒（關燈就結束）。
